Unlike some of my past formal verification blogs, this feels both useful and doable. I don't think it is that hard to get most of the core ML code numerically verified. Certainly easier and cheaper than continual learning.

"UGG: Unified Generative Geometry Model"

Video generation models don't necessarily understand the 3D geometry behind them, since video gen, depth estimation, and camera pose prediction are mostly treated as separate tasks.

This paper introduces UGG, which combines all three tasks into a single diffusion model. So by treating missing visual and geometric information as something to generate, UGG can reconstruct scene geometry from videos, generate videos from camera movements, and even search through multiple possible 3D interpretations to find the most consistent one.

On camera pose estimation, UGG reduces trajectory error better than Geo4D on ScanNet++. It also outperforms specialized video generation models on several benchmarks, especially when only limited observations are available.

https://t.co/2i59TojEs4

What happens when you add bees to an area where flowers are already scarce? 🐝

This paper tested that kind of competition in outdoor cages, where honey bees, bumble bees, and mason bees foraged alone or shared the same flowers.

Bumble bees made more flower visits in the shared cages and still produced fewer brood cells. Mason bees visited flowers about as often as before and built only a third as many nests.

A patch of flowers can look just as busy as ever even when competition is making it harder for the bees there to raise young
